problem: Let $I=[1,2]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,2-i]\times {i}.$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$

feedback.problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,1]\times [0,i].$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the intersection of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *all* the sets:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for all}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=0.5,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{0.5}=[0,1]\times [0,0.5]={(a,b)\,:\,a\in [0,1],b\in [0,0.5]}.
$$

This represents a rectangle whose vertices are at $(0,0),$ $(0,1),$ $(0.5,1),$ and $(0.5,0)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/0fef44c4b8c4911a892d7dad4502edbb80ef236553d6fddb57de1472bd44a62b.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}=[0,1]\times [0,i]={(a,b)\,:\,a\in [0,1],b\in [0,i]}
$$

is the rectangle whose vertices are at $(0,0),$ $(0,1),$ $(i,1),$ and $(i,0).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/f4602a46d3e4fc1799a475f05548ef278fdd33d354d1ec19ca4e5c5cc34cfcf8.png)

The intersection of all these rectangles is the line segments $[0,1]\times {0}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/19a2cd951a55508269a0034aec582345bf7e350ec516fe1eecac0d6bf5847981.png)
